name: securo
description: Open-source personal finance manager. Self-hosted, privacy-first.
readmeExcerpt:
Securo




Website · Demo · Roadmap · Docs · Discord · Talk to the maintainer

Finance apps want your data. This one doesn't.

We believe personal finance should actually be personal. No corporation should sit between you and your financial data. Securo is an open-source finance manager that runs on your own infrastructure, giving you full visibility into your accounts, spending, and habits, without surrendering a single byte to third parties. Take back control.

## Quick Start **Linux & macOS** (uses Docker or Podman; installs Docker if neither is present): ```bash curl -fsSL https://usesecuro.com/install.sh | bash ``` Run the same command again from the same folder to update; it finds the folder it created before, keeps the environment file and the data, and pulls the new version. **Windows:** Install [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/), then: ```bash git clone https://github.com/securo-finance/securo.git && cd securo docker compose up --build ``` Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) and create an account. That's it.

## Features - Multi-account management with running balances - Transaction management with search, filters, and CSV export - File import (OFX, QIF, CAMT, CSV) - Auto-categorization rules engine - Recurring transactions, budgets, and loan/financing tracking - Goals and savings targets with progress tracking - Asset management with valuation tracking and growth rules - Reports: Net Worth and Income vs Expenses with category sparklines - Multi-currency support with automatic FX conversion - Multi-user support with workspaces, roles, and an admin panel - Passkeys, two-factor authentication (TOTP), and OIDC single sign-on - Bank sync via providers (Pluggy, Enable Banking, SimpleFIN, extensible) - AI Agents (optional): self-hosted LLM chat with tool-use over your data ### Reporting dates and bank balances Synchronized transactions can have a reporting-date override without changing the bank's booking date. Clear the override to restore automatic attribution; later bank syncs preserve the override. Reporting periods and transaction-list dates follow the override. Account running balances and posted cash-flow balance movements still follow the bank date (or the effective movement date in accrual mode). A posted expense attributed to a future period appears in that period's cash-flow outflow, but is not deducted from the projected balance a second time. Pending card rows retain their manually selected bill date for forecast outflow and projected balance timing, including in cash mode. The calendar offers separate reporting-date and bank-date views. Moved rows retain their original bank date in the transaction list. ## Optional capabilities Everything beyond the core is off by default, needs a single env flag, and costs nothing until you turn it on. Full setup guides live in the [documentation](https://docs.usesecuro.com/): - **Bank sync**: Pluggy for Brazilian banks, Enable Banking for ~2500 European PSD2 banks, and SimpleFIN for US and international banks. [Setup guides](https://docs.usesecuro.com/docs/features/bank-sync/) Administrators can also set the credentials in the app, under **Admin Settings → Bank connections**, without a restart ([provider settings](docs/provider-settings.md)). - **Login & security**: passkeys (Touch ID, Face ID, security keys), TOTP two-factor, and OIDC single sign-on with account linking and provider role sync. Signing out also ends the provider's session (RP-initiated logout, using its `end_session_endpoint` or `OIDC_LOGOUT_URL`). [Guide](https://docs.usesecuro.com/docs/features/security/) - **Exchange rates**: a free [Open Exchange Rates](https://openexchangerates.org/) key, set in `.env` or under **Admin Settings → Exchange rates**, enables automatic currency conversion; without one, cross-currency amounts fall back to 1:1 with a visual warning. [Details](https://docs.usesecuro.com/docs/deployment/docker/) - **Timezone**: balances, budgets, and due dates turn over at midnight in your application timezone, set once in Admin Settings, with per-workspace overrides. [Details](https://docs.usesecuro.com/docs/features/workspaces/) - **Attachment storage**: attachments and invoice logos stay on local disk by default; set `STORAGE_PROVIDER=s3` to keep them in a private S3-compatible bucket instead. [Guide](https://docs.usesecuro.com/docs/deployment/docker/#storing-attachments-in-s3) - **Plugins**: install community plugins into a workspace from the plugin catalog, with a preview before anything changes. A plugin's icon is served by Securo, which reads it from the catalog, so browsing never sends your browser anywhere else. Data plugins add categories and rules and need only `PLUGINS_ENABLED=true`. Plugins with code, such as sync from a service you use, also need the `plugins` Compose profile: they run in their own containers, without the core secrets or the database, and can reach only the hosts they declare. - **AI Agents**: self-hosted assistants over your data, multi-provider, with tool use and a per-agent knowledge base. [Guide](https://docs.usesecuro.com/docs/features/agents/) ## AI-Assisted Development Parts of this codebase were built with help of AI. All code is human-reviewed and no data leaves your environment. Contributing with AI is welcome. We review the author, not the tool: whatever wrote the diff, you own its quality, its fit with where Securo is going, and everything that happens after it merges. See [Using AI](CONTRIBUTING.md#using-ai). ## Support Securo Securo is free and open source, and it runs entirely on your own infrastructure. If it helps you, a coffee keeps development going:

## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for setup and guidelines. Not sure where to start, or want to talk something through first? [Book 15 minutes](https://cal.com/tassio/15min) — no agenda needed. Something broken, an idea, or just what you think of Securo, all welcome. ## License This project is licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0](LICENSE). This means you can freely use, modify, and distribute this software, but any modifications — including when used as a network service (SaaS) — must also be released under the AGPL-3.0.

releases.name: v0.21.0
releases.body:
💜 **A special thank you to the people who donated to Securo: Alison, ThomasA, Rafaelcar, Patou, Felipe Affonso, Craig and 4 others who chose to stay anonymous.** Your support keeps Securo independent, supports the developers who keep working on it, and helps the whole community around it.

In this release we spent most of our time on fixes, as promised in v0.20.0: bank sync, multi-currency amounts, split shares in reports and the net worth history are all more accurate now, with Enable Banking getting the largest share of the work. We also add managed backups with scheduled runs and restore, make Securo installable as an app, let plugins add their own reports, separate cash from investment accounts in net worth, flag transactions with a reminder, and let you copy last month's budgets or turn an existing transaction into a recurring bill.

☕ **If Securo already helps you today, consider supporting it.** [Buy us a coffee](https://www.buymeacoffee.com/usesecuro)

## Before you update

- Managed backups are written inside the containers to `/app/data/backups`, which Docker Compose now maps to `./data/backups` on the host. Set `BACKUP_HOST_PATH` to keep them somewhere else.

releases.name: v0.20.0
releases.body: In this release we made bank sync extensible: a plugin can now act as a bank provider and sync accounts, transactions, card bills and holdings through the same pipeline as Pluggy, Enable Banking and SimpleFIN, and new bank integrations will be built this way from now on. We also show the reserved balances a bank reports inside an account (Mercado Pago cofrinhos and caixinhas, for example) without adding them to your balance, record stock splits in the holding ledger, show the price history of linked recurring charges, and add Hebrew with a right-to-left layout and the Israeli New Shekel. Attachments can now live in an S3-compatible bucket. On the fixes side, every install now gets a secret key of its own instead of a public default, disconnecting a bank keeps its accounts and history, and a rate-limited account no longer stops the rest of a bank sync. releases.body:

In this release we added plugins. A plugin can bring categories, rules and themes into a workspace, or connect an outside service with its own code, and each one is installed from a catalog with a preview of what it will add. A plugin with code runs in a separate process on your server, reaches only the hosts it declares and gets a token limited to the parts of Securo it asked for. The dashboard, the reports and the themes now come from one library: arrange the dashboard's widgets, choose which reports are listed and pick a theme, in light or dark. We also added an income & expense statement in Reports, spending progress on the Budgets page, a reporting date you can change on synced transactions, in-app settings for bank and exchange-rate providers, and recurring expense detection with a cash-flow forecast for the API and the MCP server. On the fixes side, an attachment is now served by its file extension, access tokens no longer see shares from other workspaces, and several Enable Banking syncs stop duplicating or stalling.

releases.name: v0.18.0
releases.body: In this release we added category splits: one transaction can now be divided across several categories, by amount or by percentage, and each part counts in its own category in budgets, reports, the dashboard and the category filters, while the account balance and the card bill still use the whole amount. Splits also work on recurring bills and installment series, so every generated occurrence starts already split, and they survive CSV export and import, the backup and the built-in MCP server. The MCP server can now read the investment ledger too. On the fixes side, a card or loan in credit counts as money you hold in net worth, deleting a group settlement removes the transactions it wrote, and a user who wrote invoices can be deleted without taking the workspace's billing records with them. ## Features - **Split one transaction across several categories,** by amount or percentage, with a badge in the list and "part of" rows in the dashboard drill-down. releases.name: v0.17.0
releases.body: In this release we added contract tracking for financing and loans: a mortgage, a car or other financing, a student or personal loan can now be tracked for its whole term, with the real contract behind it. Give it the amount, the rate, the term, the first payment and the amortization (Price or SAC), and Securo works out the payment schedule, splits the next payment into interest and principal, and shows when it will be paid off, both on the contract's terms and at the rate you are actually paying it down. You can break a recorded payment into principal and interest against the property it pays for, turn a bank-connected account into one of these, and enter the balance the lender reports so an indexed or renegotiated contract keeps matching it. We also added monthly budget rollover, surplus analysis and a multi-month forecast, a one-click suggestion of budget limits from earlier months, net cash-flow bars in Reports, a dashboard chart that compares a month against earlier ones, and more ways for the built-in MCP server to propose edits. On the fixes side, both sides of a group split now see the same balance, projections count only your share of a split, and open connections survive

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source, self-hosted personal finance manager designed for complete data sovereignty.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Securo is a privacy-focused personal finance and budgeting application designed to run entirely on user-controlled infrastructure. By keeping the platform self-hosted, it prevents third-party corporations and advertisers from accessing or analyzing sensitive financial data. The platform aggregates bank account information, tracks spending habits, and visualizes overall financial health through a comprehensive dashboard. It is available via a simple installation script and is strictly licensed under the AGPL-3.0 to ensure transparency. Ultimately, it provides a secure alternative to popular cloud-based budgeting applications that monetize user data.
keyFeatures: Self hosted infrastructure: Runs entirely on your own servers or home lab to guarantee complete data sovereignty.
Comprehensive dashboard: Visualizes spending habits, account balances, and financial trends in a clear interface.
Privacy focused architecture: Prevents the transmission of personal financial data to any third-party analytics engines.
Open source transparency: Licensed under AGPL 3.0, ensuring the codebase remains transparent and auditable.
Easy deployment: Offers a simple curl-to-bash installation script for quick setup on compatible systems.

useCases.title: Managing personal budgets
useCases.description: Users track their monthly expenses and income streams securely without relying on commercial SaaS products.

useCases.title: Consolidating financial data
useCases.description: Individuals bring multiple account histories into a single unified view hosted safely on a home server.

useCases.title: Enhancing data privacy
useCases.description: Privacy advocates ensure their sensitive financial records remain strictly confidential and off corporate servers.

useCases.title: Analyzing spending habits
useCases.description: Users categorize and review historical transactions using built in tools to make better financial decisions.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Securo is built for privacy advocates, home lab enthusiasts, and individuals demanding granular control over their personal finances. It appeals strongly to users who distrust commercial finance applications that monetize user data.
